culture_cards.eyebrow: Stories and Taiwan · 故事與台灣
culture_cards.title_en: Peach-wood boards, a king's two lines, an emperor's order, and the couplets of today
culture_cards.title_zh: 桃木板、國君的兩句話、皇帝的命令，和今天的春聯
culture_cards.lead_en: Two things that old books record, one famous story, and where to see couplets being written in Taiwan.
culture_cards.lead_zh: 兩件古書記下來的事、一個有名的傳說，還有在台灣哪裡看得到現場寫春聯。

cards.en: Boards of peach wood
cards.body_en: The dictionary explains that people long ago set two peach-wood boards by the door at the New Year, with the names or pictures of two gods who could catch ghosts. A Qing dynasty book about Beijing says simply, “Spring couplets are peach-wood charms.”
cards.body_zh: 教育部辭典解釋「桃符」：古代相傳有神荼、鬱壘二神能捉百鬼，所以新年時在門旁設兩塊桃木板，寫上二神的名字或畫上圖像，用來驅鬼避邪。清朝的《燕京歲時記》說：「春聯者，即桃符也。」

cards.en: “The new year brings blessings to spare”
cards.body_en: The History of Song says that every New Year's Eve the king of Shu had a scholar write words on the peach boards beside his bedroom door. One year he did not like them, so he wrote his own: 新年納餘慶，喜節號長春. A Qing scholar called this pair the oldest of its kind. Other books give slightly different words, and some scholars point to still earlier lines.
cards.body_zh: 《宋史》記載，後蜀國君孟昶「每歲除，命學士為詞，題桃符，置寢門左右」；有一年他嫌學士寫得不好，「自命筆題云：『新年納餘慶，喜節號長春。』」清朝的紀昀說這一聯「最古」。不過各書記的字句略有不同（常見的寫法是「嘉節號長春」），也有學者指出還有更早的例子。

cards.en: Did an emperor order every door to have one?
cards.body_en: A famous story says the first Ming emperor ordered every household in his capital to put up a spring couplet on New Year's Eve, and then walked the streets in plain clothes to look at them. The story comes from a Qing dynasty book of anecdotes, written long after his time, so treat it as a story.
cards.body_zh: 有個有名的故事：明太祖定都金陵後，「於除夕忽傳旨：公卿士庶家，門上須加春聯一副」，還微服出去看。這個說法出自清朝的筆記《簪雲樓雜說》（後人轉引），離明太祖的時代已經很久，所以只能當作傳說。

cards.en: Couplets written while you wait
cards.body_en: Each winter the Office of the President gives out a New Year couplet; for 2026, the Year of the Horse, the words were 七喜春來, written by the calligrapher Yu Tianci. The National Palace Museum has invited calligraphers to write couplets and diamond papers for visitors, and the Sun Yat-sen Memorial Hall has held a New Year writing event since 2005.
cards.body_zh: 總統府每年冬天都會發送新年春聯；2026 年（馬年）的賀詞是「七喜春來」，由書法家余天賜揮毫。故宮辦過新春揮毫活動，請書法老師「為民眾揮毫致贈春聯、斗方」；國父紀念館則從民國 94 年（2005）起，每年春節前都舉辦迎春揮毫。

myths.myth_en: The two lines can go on either side of the door.
myths.myth_zh: 兩句貼哪一邊都可以。
myths.fact_en: A couplet has an order. The upper line ends in an oblique tone and the lower line in a level tone, and by custom the upper line goes on the right as you face the door.
myths.fact_zh: 對聯有上下之分：上聯末字仄聲、下聯末字平聲。照習慣，面對大門時上聯貼右邊。

myths.myth_en: Third and fourth tone are always oblique; first and second tone are always level.
myths.myth_zh: 三聲、四聲一定是仄聲，一聲、二聲一定是平聲。
myths.fact_en: Mostly, but not always. The dictionary notes that the old entering tone no longer exists in Mandarin: its characters are now spread across all four tones. So 福 is second tone today but still counts as oblique.
myths.fact_zh: 大部分是，但不是全部。教育部辭典說：「現國音中已無入聲，入聲字分別歸入陰平、陽平、上聲、去聲四聲之中。」所以「福」現在唸二聲，仍然算仄聲。

myths.myth_en: Spring couplets began with an order from the first Ming emperor.
myths.myth_zh: 春聯是明太祖下令才開始有的。
myths.fact_en: That is a story from a Qing dynasty book. The History of Song already records lines written on New Year peach boards in the tenth century, about four hundred years earlier.
myths.fact_zh: 那是清朝筆記裡的故事。《宋史》已經記載十世紀時在桃符上題句，比明太祖早了大約四百年。

myths.myth_en: The character 福 must always be hung upside down.
myths.myth_zh: 「福」字一定要倒著貼。
myths.fact_en: Some people do turn it over, because 倒 (upside down) sounds like 到 (to arrive). But it is a play on words, not a rule, and customs differ from family to family.
myths.fact_zh: 有人把它倒過來貼，因為「倒」和「到」同音，代表「福到」。不過這是諧音的趣味，不是規定；每一家的習慣不一樣。

tricks.body_en: Listen to the last character of each line.
tricks.body_zh: 聽每一句的最後一個字。

tricks.title_en: Face the door: upper line on the right
tricks.body_en: The traditional way to hang a couplet.
tricks.body_zh: 傳統的貼法。

tricks.title_en: Turn the square on its corner
tricks.body_en: One lucky character: 春 or 福.
tricks.body_zh: 寫一個吉祥的字：春、福。

tricks.body_en: Wet ink runs if you hang it too soon.
tricks.body_zh: 墨還沒乾就掛起來，會往下流。

safety.en: Ink stains clothes and is very hard to wash out. Wear old clothes or an apron, and roll up your sleeves.
safety.zh: 墨沾到衣服很難洗掉：穿舊衣服或圍裙，袖子捲起來。

safety.en: Cover the desk with old newspaper, and keep the ink in a heavy, steady dish so it will not tip over.
safety.zh: 桌上先鋪舊報紙；墨要裝在重一點、放得穩的碟子裡，免得打翻。

safety.en: Press gently. Crushing the brush against the paper squashes the hairs and can split or break them.
safety.zh: 輕輕地按就好：把筆用力壓在紙上，筆毛會擠扁，也可能分岔或折斷。

safety.en: Do not put the brush, the ink, or the ink stick in your mouth, and do not lick the brush tip to shape it.
safety.zh: 毛筆、墨汁、墨條都不要放進嘴裡，也不要用嘴巴舔筆尖。

safety.en: After writing, wash the brush in clean water until the water runs clear, gently shape it into a point, and hang it tip-down or lay it flat to dry. Wash your hands, too.
safety.zh: 寫完後用清水洗筆，洗到水變清為止；輕輕把筆毛理成尖形，筆尖朝下掛起來或平放晾乾。也要洗手。

materials.en: A square of red paper, about 20 to 30 cm on each side
materials.zh: 正方形的紅紙，邊長大約 20 到 30 公分

materials.en: A large brush, ink, and old newspaper to cover the desk
materials.zh: 大一點的毛筆、墨汁，鋪桌子的舊報紙

materials.en: Scrap paper for practice
materials.zh: 練習用的廢紙

steps.en: Fold the square corner to corner both ways, then open it. The folds cross at the middle.
steps.zh: 把紅紙沿兩條對角線各摺一次再打開，摺痕交叉的地方就是正中間。

steps.en: Turn the paper so that one corner points up.
steps.zh: 把紙轉成一個角朝上。

steps.en: Practice 春 on scrap paper first, in the right stroke order. Use the practice pad on this page if you like.
steps.zh: 先在廢紙上照筆順練習「春」。也可以先用這一頁的練字板。

steps.en: Write 春 on the red paper, with the middle of the character on the cross. Let it dry flat.
steps.zh: 在紅紙上寫「春」，讓字的中心落在摺痕交叉的地方。寫完平放晾乾。

activities.tip_en: Load the brush well, but wipe off the extra ink first so it does not drip.
activities.tip_zh: 筆要蘸飽墨，但下筆前先把多餘的墨刮掉，才不會滴下來。

materials.en: Six couplets from this page, each line on its own strip of paper
materials.zh: 這一頁的六副對聯，每一句寫在一張紙條上

materials.en: Tape, and the classroom door
materials.zh: 膠帶，和教室的門

steps.en: Mix up all twelve strips. Each pair of students takes one strip and finds the partner who holds the matching line.
steps.zh: 把十二張紙條混在一起。兩人一組拿一張，去找拿著另一句的那一組。

steps.en: Say the last characters out loud and decide which line is the upper line.
steps.zh: 把兩句的末字唸出來，決定哪一句是上聯。

steps.en: Stand facing the door and hold the two lines on the correct sides. The class checks.
steps.zh: 面對教室的門，把兩句舉在正確的兩邊，請全班檢查。

steps.en: Challenge: write your own pair of four-character lines in English or Chinese.
steps.zh: 挑戰：用英文或中文，自己寫一副四個字（或四個詞）的對句。

activities.tip_en: An English couplet can match too: “Flowers open, wealth arrives; bamboo speaks, peace stays.”
activities.tip_zh: 英文也可以對仗，例如把「花開富貴，竹報平安」譯成兩句字數相當的句子。

sources.en: Spring couplets: lucky lines written on red paper at the Lunar New Year and put up on both sides of the door
sources.zh: 春聯：「農曆新年時，以紅紙書寫吉祥的聯語，張貼在門的兩旁。」
sources.src: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》「春聯」

sources.en: Couplet: two lines with the same number of characters whose words match
sources.zh: 對聯：「字數相同，用字互相對仗的兩個句子。」上聯：「對聯的前一半。」橫批：「與對聯搭配的橫幅。」
sources.src: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》「對聯」

sources.en: Peach-wood charms and the two door gods; “Spring couplets are peach-wood charms”
sources.zh: 桃符：「新年時於門旁設兩塊桃木板，上面書寫二神之名或畫上其圖像，用以驅鬼避邪」；《燕京歲時記》：「春聯者，即桃符也。」
sources.src: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》「桃符」

sources.en: Diamond paper (doufang): a square paper for lucky words, pasted on the door
sources.zh: 斗方：「用以書寫吉祥文字，貼在門上的方形紙。」
sources.src: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》「斗方」

sources.en: Level and oblique tones: level is the level tone; oblique is the rising, departing, and entering tones
sources.zh: 平仄：「平，四聲中的平聲。仄，四聲中的上、去、入三聲。」平聲：「今國音分化為陰平、陽平二類，即第一聲、第二聲。」
sources.src: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》「平仄」

sources.en: The entering tone no longer exists in Mandarin; its characters are spread across the four tones
sources.zh: 入聲：「現國音中已無入聲，入聲字分別歸入陰平、陽平、上聲、去聲四聲之中。」
sources.src: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》「入聲」

sources.en: Meng Chang wrote his own lines on the peach boards: 新年納餘慶，喜節號長春
sources.zh: 「每歲除，命學士為詞，題桃符，置寢門左右。末年，學士幸寅遜撰詞，昶以其非工，自命筆題云：『新年納餘慶，喜節號長春。』」
sources.src: 維基文庫《宋史》卷四百七十九

sources.en: Ji Yun: Meng Chang's pair is the oldest; the story of the first Ming emperor's order, quoted from a Qing book of anecdotes
sources.zh: 「楹帖始於桃符，蜀孟昶『餘慶』『長春』一聯最古」；引《簪雲樓雜說》：「春聯之設，自明孝陵昉也…於除夕忽傳旨：『公卿士庶家，門上須加春聯一副。』」
sources.src: 維基文庫 梁章鉅《楹聯叢話》卷一

sources.en: Upper line ends in an oblique tone, lower line in a level tone
sources.zh: 「對聯必有一上聯(或稱右聯)與一下聯(左聯)」「上聯最後一字必為仄聲，下聯最後一字必為平聲，更可以此分辨上下聯，以免左右掛反」
sources.src: 臺北市立麗山高中 徐茂瑋〈閒話對聯〉

sources.en: Which side: level tone (first and second tone) on the left; rising, departing, and entering tones on the right
sources.zh: 「平聲（國字注音第一、二聲）在左邊，上聲、去聲（國字注音第三、四聲）及入聲字在右邊。其中入聲字的判別方法是用台語發音，音短促而重者即是。」
sources.src: 臺北市民族國小「民族小小書法家」〈春聯的正確貼法〉

sources.en: Turning 福 or 春 upside down for the pun “has arrived”; Meng Chang's lines called the earliest spring couplet
sources.zh: 「更有人把這些字都倒過來貼，代表『福到』、『春到』…」
sources.src: 農業部兒童網〈春聯〉

sources.en: Stroke order and stroke counts: 春 has 9 strokes; 福 has 13
sources.zh: 筆順與筆畫數：「春」9 畫、「福」13 畫
sources.src: 教育部《國字標準字體筆順學習網》

sources.en: The Office of the President's New Year couplet for 2026 (Year of the Horse): 七喜春來, written by Yu Tianci
sources.zh: 總統府 115 年新春賀詞「七喜春來」，由書法名家余天賜揮毫
sources.src: 中華民國總統府新聞稿

sources.en: National Palace Museum: calligraphers write couplets and diamond papers for visitors
sources.zh: 「現場安排6位書法老師為民眾揮毫致贈春聯、斗方」
sources.src: 國立故宮博物院〈新春揮毫贈春聯活動〉

sources.en: Sun Yat-sen Memorial Hall: a New Year calligraphy event every year since 2005
sources.zh: 「自94年起，每到農曆春節前夕都會舉辦迎春揮毫活動」
sources.src: 國立國父紀念館新聞稿

sources.en: Taiwan curriculum: forms and set phrases of letters, notes, and couplets (Be-Ⅳ-2); brush writing in regular script (4-Ⅲ-5)
sources.zh: 十二年國教國語文領綱：Be-Ⅳ-2「在人際溝通方面，以書信、便條、對聯等之慣用語彙與書寫格式為主。」4-Ⅲ-5「習寫以硬筆字為主，毛筆為輔，掌握楷書形體結構的書寫方法。」
sources.src: 國家教育研究院《十二年國民基本教育課程綱要 語文領域—國語文》

sides.en: Which Line Is the Upper Line?
sides.lead_en: Here are the two lines of a couplet, in mixed-up order. Say the last character of each line out loud. The line that ends in the third or fourth tone is the upper line. (None of these six has a trap character at the end.)
sides.lead_zh: 一副對聯的兩句，順序被弄亂了。把兩句的最後一個字唸出來：末字是三聲或四聲的那一句就是上聯。（這六副的末字都沒有陷阱字。）

lessons.title: What Are the Red Seals on a Work of Calligraphy?
lessons.title_zh: 印章與篆刻：作品上的紅色印章是什麼？
lessons.blurb_en: A finished work of calligraphy is black and white, with a few small squares of red. They are seals. Watch a seal show its face, dip into red paste, and print in 3D; find out why the face must be carved backward; tell red-character seals from white-character seals; and design a seal of your own.
lessons.blurb_zh: 一件寫好的書法作品是黑白的，上面有幾個小小的紅色方塊——那是印章。在 3D 裡看印章把印面翻給你看、蘸印泥、蓋在紙上；弄懂印面為什麼要反著刻；分辨朱文和白文；再設計一方自己的印。
lessons.big_idea_en: A seal is a small block with characters carved on its face. Pressed into red paste and then onto paper, it prints the artist's name or a favorite phrase. Stamping flips left and right, so the face is carved as a mirror image. Raised characters print red, and cut-in characters print white.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 印章是一小塊刻了字的材料。蘸上紅色的印泥再蓋在紙上，就印出作者的名字或喜歡的句子。蓋印會把左右翻過來，所以印面要反著刻。凸起來的字蓋出來是紅的（朱文），凹下去的字蓋出來是白的（白文）。

lab.title_en: The Face Is Backward, the Print Is Not
lab.title_zh: 印面是反的，蓋出來才是正的
lab.how_en: Drag to turn, and scroll or pinch to zoom. Press Stamp it: the seal shows you its face, dips into the red paste, and prints on the paper. Change the character, switch between red and white characters, and then try carving the face “the way you read it” to see what goes wrong.
lab.how_zh: 拖曳可以旋轉，滾輪或雙指可以縮放。按「蓋印」：印章先把印面翻給你看，再蘸印泥，蓋在紙上。可以換字、換朱文或白文，再試試「照正的刻」，看看會出什麼問題。

legend.en: Red: seal paste
legend.zh: 紅色：印泥

legend.en: Yellow label: the face of the seal
legend.zh: 黃色標籤：印面

legend.en: The character on the seal is in small seal script
legend.zh: 印面上的字是小篆

lab.scale_en: A teaching model. The seal, the paste, and the paper are our own simple shapes, and the seal is drawn larger than most real ones. The characters on the seal are our own tracings of small seal script from Lesson 5. The speckles in the print only suggest that paste never prints perfectly evenly. The character 永 on the paper is the regular-script model from Lesson 3.
lab.scale_zh: 這是教學用的示意模型。印章、印泥和紙都是我們畫的簡單造型，印章畫得比一般的印大。印面上的字是第五課我們自己描的小篆。印文上的小白點只是示意：印泥不會蓋得完全均勻。紙上的「永」是第三課的楷書範字。
lab.credit_html: Model and seal drawings are drawn and programmed by My Culture Connect; the seal-script characters are our own tracings from Lesson 5. · 模型與印章圖樣由人師教育協會自繪、自寫；小篆字形是第五課自己描的。

paras: Look at a finished work of calligraphy. The characters are black and the paper is pale, but somewhere, often near the writer's name, there are small squares of red. They are the prints of seals.

A seal is a small block, often of stone, with characters carved on one end. That end is called the face. The writer presses the face into a thick red paste and then onto the paper. The print says who made the work, or adds a few words the writer loves.

Here is the strange part. If you look at the face of a seal, the characters are backward. Stamping flips left and right, like a mirror. So the carver writes the characters in mirror image, and the print comes out the right way round.

There are two ways to carve. In a red-character seal, the carver cuts away everything except the lines, so the lines stand up and print in red. In a white-character seal, the carver cuts only the lines, so they stay white inside a block of red.

Most seals use seal script, the old script with even, curving lines. That is where its English name comes from. Seals are far older than paper. Long ago, letters were written on strips of bamboo or wood, tied shut, and closed with a lump of clay. The sender pressed a seal into the clay, so nobody could open the letter in secret.

Seals are still part of life in Taiwan. Many people have a small seal with their name on it, and the law says that a seal used in place of a signature counts the same as signing. In this lesson, stamp a seal in 3D, play red or white, and design a seal of your own.
paras_zh: 看看一件寫好的書法作品。字是黑的，紙是淺色的，可是在某個地方——常常在作者名字的旁邊——有幾個小小的紅色方塊。那是印章蓋出來的印。
印章是一小塊材料，常常是石頭，其中一頭刻了字，那一面叫印面。作者把印面按進濃稠的紅色印泥，再蓋在紙上。蓋出來的印告訴大家這件作品是誰寫的，或是加上幾個作者喜歡的字。
奇怪的地方來了：仔細看印面，上面的字是反的。蓋印會把左右翻過來，就像照鏡子一樣。所以刻印的人要把字反著寫上去，蓋出來才會是正的。
刻法有兩種。「朱文」是把線條以外的地方都刻掉，線條凸出來，蓋出來字是紅的。「白文」是只把線條刻掉，蓋出來是一塊紅色，字留白。
印章大多用篆書——線條勻稱、彎彎的古老字體；篆書的英文名字 seal script 就是這樣來的。印章比紙古老得多。很久以前，信寫在竹片或木片上，綁好以後，在繩結上按一團泥，寄信的人再把印章蓋在泥上（封泥），這樣就沒有人能偷偷拆開。
在台灣，印章到今天還是生活的一部分。很多人有一顆刻著自己名字的小印章；法律也規定，用印章代替簽名，效力和簽名一樣。這一課，在 3D 裡蓋一方印，玩「朱文還是白文？」，再設計一方自己的印。
questions: Why are the characters on the face of a seal carved backward?
What is the difference between a red-character seal and a white-character seal?
Before paper, what did people press their seals into?
answers: Because stamping flips left and right, like a mirror. A mirror-image face prints the right way round.
In a red-character seal the lines stand up and print in red. In a white-character seal the lines are cut in, so they stay white inside a block of red.
A lump of clay that closed a tied bundle of bamboo or wooden strips.

vocab.ex: The letter had a red wax seal on the back.
vocab.exzh: 那封信的背面有一個紅色的蠟封。

vocab.ex: The librarian stamped the date in my book.
vocab.exzh: 圖書館員在我的書上蓋了日期。

vocab.ex: Words look backward in a mirror.
vocab.exzh: 鏡子裡的字看起來是反的。

vocab.ex: Can you say the alphabet backward?
vocab.exzh: 你能把字母倒著唸嗎？

vocab.ex: Mix the flour and water into a thick paste.
vocab.exzh: 把麵粉和水拌成濃稠的糊。

vocab.ex: The coin has raised letters around the edge.
vocab.exzh: 這枚硬幣的邊緣有凸起來的字。

vocab.exzh: 請在表格最下面簽名。

parts.meta_en: Lines stand up · also called yang characters
parts.meta_zh: 線條凸出來・也叫陽文
parts.text_en: Everything except the lines is cut away. The raised lines pick up the paste, so the characters print red.
parts.text_zh: 線條以外的地方都刻掉。凸起來的線條沾到印泥，蓋出來字是紅的。

parts.meta_en: Lines are cut in · also called yin characters
parts.meta_zh: 線條凹下去・也叫陰文
parts.text_en: Only the lines are cut away. The paste cannot reach them, so they stay white inside a block of red.
parts.text_zh: 只把線條刻掉。印泥沾不到凹下去的線條，蓋出來是一塊紅色、字留白。

parts.text_en: This is what the carver cuts. Compare it with the first card: left and right are swapped.
parts.text_zh: 這是刻印的人刻出來的樣子。和第一張卡比一比：左右相反。

parts.meta_en: Face carved the way you read it
parts.text_en: If the face is carved the way you read it, the print comes out backward, like this.
parts.text_zh: 如果印面照正的刻，蓋出來就是反的，像這樣。

lessons.parts_note_en: All four show 馬 (horse) in small seal script. Tap a card to see it happen in 3D.
lessons.parts_note_zh: 四張卡都是小篆的「馬」。點卡片，在模型裡看它怎麼蓋出來。

pad.lead_en: Before carving, the carver writes the characters. Trace these six in small seal script. Seal-script lines stay the same width from beginning to end, so keep a slow, even speed.
pad.lead_zh: 刻印之前要先寫字。描寫這六個小篆。小篆的線條從頭到尾一樣粗，所以速度要慢、要平均。

tips.en: Keep every line the same width: no heavy starts and no pointed ends.
tips.zh: 每一條線都一樣粗：起筆不加重，收筆不出尖。

tips.en: Curves should be round and smooth, like bent wire.
tips.zh: 轉彎要圓、要順，像彎過的鐵絲。

tips.en: When you finish, hold your screen up to a mirror. That is what the seal face would look like.
tips.zh: 寫完以後，把螢幕拿去照鏡子——鏡子裡的樣子，就是印面的樣子。

culture_cards.lead_zh: 兩件古書裡的事、一件在台灣看得到的寶物，還有今天台灣人怎麼用印章。

cards.en: A lump of clay with a seal on it
cards.body_en: The dictionary explains sealing clay: before paper, messages were written on strips of bamboo or wood. To stop anyone from opening them in secret, the knot of the cord was packed with clay and stamped with a seal. A museum in Taipei shows wooden address tablets with a small slot cut to hold the clay.
cards.body_zh: 教育部辭典解釋「封泥」：「古人未有紙時，以簡素傳遞信息，為防私拆，在繩結開啟處，以泥封緊，加蓋印章。」中研院史語所歷史文物陳列館展出的「檢」，就是「附有封泥槽，可加蓋封泥印章，以達密封機能之簡牘」。

cards.en: The word only emperors could use
cards.body_en: A Han dynasty book says that before the Qin dynasty anyone might have a seal of gold or jade, but from the Qin on, only the emperor's seal was called 璽, and only his could be made of jade. Everyone else's was simply called 印.
cards.body_zh: 東漢蔡邕的《獨斷》說：「璽者印也，印者信也。」「秦以前民皆以金玉為印……秦以來天子獨以印稱璽，又獨以玉，羣臣莫敢用也。」教育部辭典也說：璽「秦以前泛指諸侯、卿大夫、從吏的印章，秦以後則專指帝王的印章」。

cards.en: An emperor's birthday seal, in Taipei
cards.zh: 台北故宮的「古稀天子之寶」
cards.body_en: The National Palace Museum keeps a jade seal made for the Qianlong Emperor in 1780, the year he turned seventy. It is carved from one piece of green jade, 12.8 centimeters on each side, with two dragons on top. Its six seal-script characters mean “treasure of the Son of Heaven at seventy.”
cards.body_zh: 台北故宮藏有一方乾隆皇帝的玉璽，做於乾隆四十五年（1780），那一年他七十歲。故宮說它「全器選用整塊碧玉琢製而成，印面為正方形，雙龍鈕」，長寬各 12.8 公分；「印面琢三行六字篆書：『古稀天子之寶』」。

cards.en: The seal in your drawer
cards.body_en: In Taiwan, a person can register one personal seal at the household registration office. The rules say its face must be between 1 and 3 centimeters across, and it cannot be made of rubber or other soft material that changes shape. The Civil Code says a seal used in place of a signature has the same effect as signing.
cards.body_zh: 在台灣，每個人可以到戶政事務所登記一顆印鑑。規定是「以一種為限」，「印面之長、寬或直徑須 1 公分以上未逾 3 公分，且不得使用原子章或橡膠等易變形材質」。《民法》第 3 條也規定：「如有用印章代簽名者，其蓋章與簽名生同等之效力。」

myths.myth_en: The characters on the face of a seal read the same as the print.
myths.myth_zh: 印面上的字和蓋出來的字是一樣的。
myths.fact_en: They are mirror images. Stamping flips left and right, so the carver writes the characters backward on the stone.
myths.fact_zh: 兩者左右相反。蓋印會把左右翻過來，所以刻印的人要把字反著寫在印石上。

myths.myth_en: A “red-character seal” is carved from red stone.
myths.myth_zh: 「朱文印」是用紅色的石頭刻的。
myths.fact_en: The name describes the print, not the stone. In a red-character seal the lines are raised, so the characters print red. The dictionary gives the old rule: raised characters are red characters, and cut-in characters are white characters.
myths.fact_zh: 「朱文」說的是蓋出來的樣子，不是石頭的顏色。朱文的線條凸出來，所以字蓋出來是紅的。教育部辭典引古人的話：「刻之印章，則陽文曰朱文，陰文曰白文。」

myths.myth_en: In old China, only emperors had seals.
myths.myth_zh: 古時候只有皇帝才有印章。
myths.fact_en: Only the word 璽 was kept for the emperor's seal, from the Qin dynasty on. Officials and ordinary people had seals too, called 印.
myths.fact_zh: 秦以後只有「璽」這個字專指皇帝的印。官員和一般人也有印章，叫「印」。

myths.myth_en: Seal paste is just red ink.
myths.myth_zh: 印泥就是紅色的墨水。
myths.fact_en: It is a thick paste, not a liquid. Taiwan's school dictionary says it is made of cinnabar, oil, and mugwort fiber.
myths.fact_zh: 印泥是濃稠的泥狀顏料，不是液體。《國語辭典簡編本》說它「用硃砂和油及艾絨製成」。

tricks.body_en: Stamping flips left and right.
tricks.body_zh: 蓋印會把左右翻過來。

tricks.title_en: Raised prints red, cut-in prints white
tricks.title_zh: 凸的是朱文，凹的是白文
tricks.body_en: Red characters or white characters.
tricks.body_zh: 字是紅的，或字是白的。

tricks.body_en: That is why it is called seal carving.
tricks.body_zh: 所以叫「篆刻」。

tricks.title_en: Opening seal upper right, corner seal lower right
tricks.title_zh: 引首章右上，壓角章右下
tricks.body_en: Where extra seals go on a work.
tricks.body_zh: 作品上閒章蓋的位置。

safety.en: Real seal paste is made with cinnabar and oil. Do not put it near your mouth, and wash your hands after stamping.
safety.zh: 真的印泥是用硃砂和油做的。不要靠近嘴巴，蓋完印要洗手。

safety.en: Seal paste stains clothes and is hard to wash out. Wear old clothes or an apron.
safety.zh: 印泥沾到衣服很難洗掉：穿舊衣服或圍裙。

safety.en: Carving knives are sharp. In class, press lines into craft foam with a pencil instead of cutting stone.
safety.zh: 刻刀很利。課堂上改用鉛筆在泡棉片上壓出線條，不要刻石頭。

safety.en: Let each print dry before you stack the papers.
safety.zh: 印乾了再把紙疊起來。

materials.en: A small square of craft foam (about 3 cm), glued to a bottle cap or a block
materials.zh: 一小塊泡棉片（大約 3 公分見方），黏在瓶蓋或小木塊上

materials.en: Thin paper and a soft pencil
materials.zh: 薄紙和軟一點的鉛筆

materials.en: A washable red stamp pad and white paper
materials.zh: 可水洗的紅色印台和白紙

steps.en: On the thin paper, draw a square the size of your foam and write one simple character inside it, dark and thick.
steps.zh: 在薄紙上畫一個和泡棉一樣大的方框，在裡面寫一個簡單的字，寫黑一點、粗一點。

steps.en: Turn the paper over onto the foam and rub the back. The pencil marks move to the foam in mirror image.
steps.zh: 把紙翻過來蓋在泡棉上，在背面磨一磨。鉛筆的痕跡會反著印到泡棉上。

steps.en: Press the lines deep into the foam with the pencil. You have made a white-character seal.
steps.zh: 用鉛筆把線條深深地壓進泡棉裡。你做了一顆白文印。

steps.en: Press the seal on the stamp pad, then on white paper. Does your character read the right way?
steps.zh: 蘸印台，蓋在白紙上。你的字是正的嗎？

activities.tip_en: Start with a character that is not the same on both sides, such as 人 or 月, so you can see the flip.
activities.tip_zh: 先選左右不對稱的字，例如「人」或「月」，才看得出有沒有翻過來。

materials.en: The picture of the snow letter on this page, on a screen or printed
materials.zh: 這一頁的〈快雪時晴帖〉圖片（用螢幕看或印出來）

materials.en: A small mirror
materials.zh: 一面小鏡子

steps.en: In pairs, count how many red seals you can find in two minutes.
steps.zh: 兩人一組，兩分鐘內數數看找得到幾方紅色的印。

steps.en: Sort them: which have red characters, and which have white characters?
steps.zh: 分類：哪些是朱文，哪些是白文？

steps.en: Pick one seal and hold the mirror beside it. The mirror shows what its face looks like.
steps.zh: 選一方印，把鏡子放在旁邊。鏡子裡的樣子，就是那顆印章的印面。

steps.en: Talk about it: why would an owner want to stamp a seal on a famous work? Would you?
steps.zh: 討論：為什麼擁有名作的人會想在上面蓋自己的印？換成是你，你會蓋嗎？

activities.tip_en: There is no single right answer to the last question. Collectors and museums think about it differently today.
activities.tip_zh: 最後一題沒有標準答案。今天的收藏家和博物館，想法和古人不一樣。

sources.en: Seal carving: seals mostly imitate Qin and Han seals and use seal script; the characters are written first and then carved
sources.zh: 篆刻：「雕刻印章。因印章多模仿秦漢古印，採用大小篆體，先寫後刻，故稱為『篆刻』。」
sources.src: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》「篆刻」

sources.en: Red characters: raised characters on a seal; “raised characters are called red characters, and cut-in characters are called white characters”
sources.zh: 朱文：「印章上鐫刻凸出的文字，即陽文。」引楊慎：「刻之印章，則陽文曰朱文，陰文曰白文。」
sources.src: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》「朱文」

sources.en: White characters: the cut-in characters or patterns on a seal or vessel
sources.zh: 白文：「鏤刻器物或印章，所凹下的文字或花紋部分，稱為『白文』。……也稱為『陰文』。」
sources.src: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》「白文」

sources.en: Seal paste: a paste-like pigment made of cinnabar and oil (the school dictionary adds mugwort fiber)
sources.zh: 印泥：「蓋印時所用的泥狀顏料。用硃砂和油製成。」《國語辭典簡編本》：「用硃砂和油及艾絨製成。」
sources.src: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》「印泥」

sources.en: Seal paste in the school dictionary: cinnabar, oil, and mugwort fiber
sources.zh: 「蓋印章時所沾取的泥狀顏料。用硃砂和油及艾絨製成。」
sources.src: 教育部《國語辭典簡編本》「印泥」（教育百科）

sources.en: Sealing clay: before paper, the knot on a bundle of slips was packed with clay and stamped
sources.zh: 封泥：「古人未有紙時，以簡素傳遞信息，為防私拆，在繩結開啟處，以泥封緊，加蓋印章，故稱為『封泥』。」
sources.src: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》「封泥」

sources.en: A wooden tablet with a slot for sealing clay
sources.zh: 檢：「附有封泥槽，可加蓋封泥印章，以達密封機能之簡牘。」
sources.src: 中央研究院歷史語言研究所歷史文物陳列館

sources.en: 璽: before the Qin, the seals of lords and officials; after the Qin, only the seals of emperors
sources.zh: 璽：「秦以前泛指諸侯、卿大夫、從吏的印章，秦以後則專指帝王的印章。」
sources.src: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》「璽」

sources.en: Cai Yong: “from the Qin on, only the Son of Heaven's seal was called 璽, and only his was of jade”
sources.zh: 「璽者印也，印者信也」「秦以來天子獨以印稱璽，又獨以玉，羣臣莫敢用也。」
sources.src: 維基文庫 蔡邕《獨斷》

sources.en: Opening seal (upper right), corner seal (lower right), leisure seals, collector's seals, and the signature block
sources.zh: 引首章：「書法作品上鈐蓋在右上方的一種閒章。」壓角章（151963）：「鈐蓋在右下方」；閒章（108043）；鑑藏印（93737）：「蓋在書畫上的印章。表示作品經過鈐印者的鑑定收藏。」落款（66693）
sources.src: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》「引首章」

sources.en: A seal on a work is proof of who made it
sources.zh: 「書家在作品上鈐印，具有證明取信之作用。」
sources.src: 臺北市民族國小「民族小小書法家」〈落款與用印〉

sources.en: Timely Clearing After Snowfall: the museum's record of its inscriptions and seals
sources.zh: 〈快雪時晴帖〉典藏頁：題跋、收傳印記與鑑藏寶璽
sources.src: 國立故宮博物院典藏資料檢索（故書000141）

sources.en: Jade seal of the Qianlong Emperor, 1780: one piece of green jade, 12.8 cm square, two dragons on top, six seal-script characters
sources.zh: 「古稀天子之寶」玉璽：「全器選用整塊碧玉琢製而成，印面為正方形，雙龍鈕…印面琢三行六字篆書」「乾隆庚子即乾隆四十五年（1780），這年清高宗七十歲。」
sources.src: 國立故宮博物院典藏資料檢索（故玉006652）

sources.en: Registering a personal seal in Taiwan: one seal only; 1 to 3 cm; no rubber or other material that changes shape
sources.zh: 「申請登記之印鑑以一種為限」「印鑑章印面之長、寬或直徑須 1 公分以上未逾 3 公分，且不得使用原子章或橡膠等易變形材質。」
sources.src: 內政部戶政司〈印鑑登記及印鑑證明業務〉

sources.en: Civil Code, Article 3: a seal used in place of a signature has the same effect as signing
sources.zh: 《民法》第 3 條：「如有用印章代簽名者，其蓋章與簽名生同等之效力。」
sources.src: 全國法規資料庫

sources.en: Taiwan curriculum: know stories of famous calligraphers (4-Ⅱ-8); appreciate the layout and style of calligraphy (4-Ⅳ-5). Seal carving itself is not listed in the curriculum.
sources.zh: 十二年國教國語文領綱：4-Ⅱ-8「知道古今書法名家的故事。」4-Ⅳ-5「欣賞書法的行款和布局、行氣及風格。」（課綱沒有列篆刻；這一課是書法的延伸）
sources.src: 國家教育研究院《十二年國民基本教育課程綱要 語文領域—國語文》

sheets.eyebrow: On a Real Work · 真的作品上
sheets.en: A letter of four lines, crowded with seals
sheets.zh: 只有四行字的信，蓋滿了印
sheets.lead_en: This is Wang Xizhi's snow letter from Lesson 10. The black writing is only four lines. Everything red was added later by emperors and collectors who owned it, each one leaving a seal to say “this passed through my hands.”
sheets.lead_zh: 這是第十課看過的〈快雪時晴帖〉。黑色的字只有四行；紅色的都是後來擁有過它的皇帝和收藏家蓋上去的，每一方印都在說：「這件作品經過我的手。」

items.alt_en: Timely Clearing After Snowfall, with many red seals around four lines of writing
items.alt_zh: 〈快雪時晴帖〉：四行字的周圍蓋了許多紅色的印
items.en: Collectors' seals
items.text_en: The dictionary calls these collector's seals: seals on a work that show it was examined and kept by the person who stamped it. The museum's record for this letter lists dozens of them, including seals of the Qianlong Emperor. Can you find a white-character seal and a red-character seal?
items.text_zh: 教育部辭典說「鑑藏印」是「蓋在書畫上的印章。表示作品經過鈐印者的鑑定收藏」。故宮為這件作品記錄的印有好幾十種，其中包括乾隆皇帝的印。你找得到一方白文印和一方朱文印嗎？
items.credit_html: 晉王羲之快雪時晴帖 冊。國立故宮博物院，台北，CC BY 4.0 @ www.npm.gov.tw（經裁切）

sealkind.lead_en: Here is the print of a seal. Are the characters red, with the paper showing around them? Or are they white, inside a block of red? Eight rounds.
sealkind.lead_zh: 這是一方印蓋出來的樣子。字是紅的、周圍露出紙？還是字是白的、在一塊紅色裡面？一共八題。

sealdesign.lead_en: Choose a character, the kind of seal, and the shape. The left picture shows the face you would carve; the right picture shows what it prints. You can save the print as a picture.
sealdesign.lead_zh: 選一個字、朱文或白文、方的或圓的。左邊是你要刻的印面，右邊是蓋出來的樣子。可以把印存成圖片。

tips.en: Look at 馬, 人, or 月: the face and the print are mirror images of each other.
tips.zh: 看「馬」「人」或「月」：印面和蓋出來的印，左右正好相反。

tips.en: Now choose 山 or 日. They are almost the same on both sides, so the flip is hard to see.
tips.zh: 再選「山」或「日」。它們左右幾乎對稱，所以看不太出來有沒有翻過來。

tips.en: Switch between red and white characters. Which one would be more work to carve?
tips.zh: 切換朱文和白文。哪一種刻起來比較費工？

lessons.title: Why Do People Copy Sutras by Hand?
lessons.blurb_en: Before printing, every book was copied by hand, and Buddhist texts called sutras were copied with special care. People still copy them today, slowly, one character in each square. Watch a brush copy a line of the Heart Sutra in 3D, compare slow writing with hurried writing, find the right square, and copy five characters yourself.
lessons.blurb_zh: 還沒有印刷術的時候，每一本書都是用手抄的；佛教的經典抄得特別用心。直到今天還有很多人抄經：慢慢地，一格一個字。在 3D 裡看毛筆抄〈心經〉的一句，比較「慢而勻」和「趕著寫」，找出下一個字該寫的格子，再自己抄五個字。
lessons.big_idea_en: To copy a sutra is to write out a Buddhist text by hand, slowly and carefully, one character in each square, from top to bottom and from right to left. Long ago this was how books were made. Today many people still do it, as a way to show respect and to practice paying attention.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 抄經就是用手把佛教的經典一個字一個字抄下來：慢慢地、仔細地，一格一個字，由上到下、由右到左。很久以前，書就是這樣做出來的。今天還有很多人抄經，用來表達恭敬，也練習專注。

lab.how_en: Drag to turn, and scroll or pinch to zoom. The brush copies one line of the Heart Sutra, 色即是空，空即是色: down the first column on the right, then down the next column to its left. Then choose In a hurry and compare the two pages.
lab.how_zh: 拖曳可以旋轉，滾輪或雙指可以縮放。毛筆抄〈心經〉的一句「色即是空，空即是色」：先寫最右邊那一行，由上往下，再換左邊一行。接著選「趕著寫」，比較兩張紙有什麼不一樣。
lab.breath_en: A slow rhythm, four seconds in and four seconds out. Some people like to breathe slowly while they copy.
lab.breath_zh: 慢慢的節奏：四秒吸氣、四秒吐氣。有些人抄寫的時候喜歡這樣慢慢呼吸。

legend.en: Yellow label: where the first character goes
legend.zh: 黃色標籤：第一個字寫的地方

legend.en: Dark lines: the ruled columns of sutra paper
legend.zh: 深色的線：抄經紙的直行界線

legend.en: The circle: a slow rhythm to breathe with
legend.zh: 圓圈：跟著慢慢呼吸的節奏

lab.scale_en: A teaching model. The eight characters are one line of the Heart Sutra in the translation of Xuanzang; the whole text has 260 characters. The characters are our own brush strokes in regular script, with the stroke order of Taiwan's Ministry of Education. The brush is drawn much larger than the small brush used for real sutra copying, and real squares are only a centimeter or two wide. “In a hurry” is our own sketch of what rushing does, and the evenness score only measures how much each character's size, place, and tilt differ from the even page. The minutes are worked out from the model's speed; real people write at many different speeds.
lab.scale_zh: 這是教學用的示意模型。這八個字是玄奘譯〈心經〉裡的一句；全經正文 260 個字。字是我們自己畫的楷書，筆順依教育部。毛筆畫得比真正抄經用的小楷筆大很多，真的格子也只有一兩公分寬。「趕著寫」是我們自己畫的示意；整齊度只是量每個字的大小、位置、歪斜和「慢而勻」那一頁差多少。幾分鐘是照模型的速度算的，真人寫字的速度各不相同。
lab.credit_html: Model, stroke data, and the writing engine are drawn and programmed by My Culture Connect. The line 色即是空，空即是色 is from the Heart Sutra, T08 no. 251, CBETA. · 模型、筆畫資料與寫字引擎由人師教育協會自繪、自寫。「色即是空，空即是色」出自《般若波羅蜜多心經》（大正藏第 8 冊 No. 251），經文依 CBETA 電子佛典。

paras: Imagine a world with no printers and no copy machines. If you wanted a book, someone had to write out every word by hand. For hundreds of years, that is how the Buddhist texts called sutras were passed on. Trained copyists wrote them on long rolls of paper with ruled columns, one small, neat character after another.

Even after printing was invented, people went on copying sutras by hand, and many still do. The sutras themselves speak of writing them out as a good thing to do. For the people who copy, it is a way to show respect for the words, and a way to practice paying attention.

The rules are simple. Sit up straight. Write one character in each square. Start at the top of the column on the right, write down to the bottom, and then move one column to the left. Do not hurry. Try to make every character the same size, in the middle of its square.

The most copied text is probably the Heart Sutra. It is very short: the translation by the Tang dynasty monk Xuanzang has only 260 characters. Its best-known line has eight characters: 色即是空，空即是色, “form is emptiness, emptiness is form.” People have thought about that line for more than a thousand years. In this lesson, we simply write it.

One famous copyist was Master Hongyi. Before he became a monk in 1918, he was an art and music teacher named Li Shutong. As a monk he gave up most of his arts, but he kept on writing sutras and short sayings to give to people. He said that what his writing shows is calm and quiet.

You do not have to be Buddhist to try the method. Monks in old Europe copied books by hand too, and so did scribes in many other traditions. Copying any text you care about, slowly and neatly, is good practice for the hand and for the mind.
paras_zh: 想像一個沒有印表機、也沒有影印機的世界。想要一本書，就得有人用手把每一個字抄下來。好幾百年裡，佛教的經典就是這樣流傳的。受過訓練的抄寫人（經生）把經文寫在畫了直行界線的長卷上，一個接一個，又小又整齊。
印刷術發明以後，人們還是繼續用手抄經，直到今天。經典裡就把「書寫」經文說成一件值得做的事。對抄經的人來說，這是對經文表達恭敬的方式，也是練習專注的方法。
規矩很簡單。坐正。一格寫一個字。從最右邊那一行的最上面開始，往下寫到底，再往左換一行。不要趕。每個字盡量一樣大，寫在格子的正中間。
最多人抄的大概是〈心經〉。它非常短：唐朝玄奘法師翻譯的本子只有 260 個字。其中最有名的一句是八個字：「色即是空，空即是色。」一千多年來，人們一直在思考這句話。這一課，我們只是把它寫下來。
弘一大師是很有名的一位抄經人。1918 年出家以前，他叫李叔同，是美術和音樂老師。出家以後，他放下了大部分的藝術，卻繼續寫經、寫字送給人結緣。他說自己的字要表現的是平淡、恬靜。
不是佛教徒，也可以試試這個方法。古時候歐洲的修士同樣用手抄書，許多別的傳統也有抄寫經典的人。把一段你珍惜的文字慢慢地、整齊地抄下來，對手和對心都是很好的練習。
questions: Before printing, how were sutras passed on?
On a sutra page, where does the first character go, and which way does the writing move?
What did Master Hongyi keep doing after he became a monk?
answers: Copyists wrote them out by hand on long rolls of paper with ruled columns.
At the top of the column on the right. The writing goes down each column, and the columns go from right to left.
He kept on writing sutras and short sayings to give to people.

vocab.ex: The monk read a sutra aloud every morning.
vocab.exzh: 那位法師每天早上誦一部經。

vocab.ex: Write the numbers in the left column.
vocab.exzh: 把數字寫在左邊那一欄。

vocab.ex: Color every other square on the board.
vocab.exzh: 把棋盤上的格子每隔一格塗上顏色。

vocab.ex: Please pay attention to the road.
vocab.exzh: 請注意路況。

vocab.ex: We show respect by listening when others speak.
vocab.exzh: 別人說話的時候專心聽，就是表示尊重。

vocab.ex: The lake was calm in the early morning.
vocab.exzh: 清晨的湖面很平靜。

vocab.ex: The monks get up before the sun rises.
vocab.exzh: 出家人在日出以前就起床了。

vocab.ex: There is no need to hurry; we have plenty of time.
vocab.exzh: 不用趕，我們時間很多。

Where does a sutra page begin?

pad.lead_en: Choose one of the five characters and trace it in the order of the blue numbers. The stopwatch shows how long you took. This time, slower is better: try to match the demo or take even longer.
pad.lead_zh: 從五個字裡選一個，照藍色數字的順序描寫。碼表會告訴你花了多久。這一次是越慢越好：試試看和示範一樣久，或更久。

tips.en: Sit up straight and take one slow breath before the first stroke.
tips.zh: 坐正，下第一筆以前先慢慢呼吸一次。

tips.en: Finish each stroke completely before you start the next one.
tips.zh: 每一筆寫完整了，再寫下一筆。

tips.en: Write 心 three times. Is the third one the same size as the first?
tips.zh: 把「心」寫三次。第三個和第一個一樣大嗎？

links.note_zh: 抄得好，從每個字照筆順寫開始。

links.note_zh: 最後一個字寫完，抄經的人會落款、蓋印。

culture_cards.eyebrow: History and Taiwan · 歷史與台灣
culture_cards.title_en: Before printing, a sealed cave, a teacher who became a monk, and sutras in Taiwan
culture_cards.title_zh: 印刷以前、封起來的洞窟、出家的老師，和台灣的寫經
culture_cards.lead_en: Where the custom comes from, and where you can meet it today.
culture_cards.lead_zh: 這個習俗從哪裡來，今天又在哪裡遇得到。

cards.en: A job called “sutra copyist”
cards.body_en: A study from National Taiwan University explains that before printing was invented, old books all depended on clerks and copyists, and that Buddhist sutra copyists in the Northern Wei period were called jingsheng. The Diamond Sutra itself praises “writing out, keeping, reading, and reciting” the text.
cards.body_zh: 臺大的一篇研究說：「印刷術發明以前，古代的典籍都有賴書吏或經生抄寫」，佛教的寫經生在北魏時期就叫「經生」。《金剛經》裡也稱讚「書寫、受持、讀誦、為人解說」這部經。

cards.en: A cave full of hand-copied scrolls
cards.body_en: The dictionary records that a stone chamber at Dunhuang, on the old Silk Road, was found in 1900. Inside were a great many Buddhist texts hand-copied from the Six Dynasties to the Five Dynasties. Many were taken abroad. Taiwan's National Central Library keeps 142 Dunhuang items today.
cards.body_zh: 教育部辭典記載，絲路上的敦煌石室在清光緒二十六年（1900）被發現，裡面「藏六朝、隋、唐及五代人手寫佛教經典及其他藝術品甚富」，後來許多被帶到國外。今天台灣的國家圖書館藏有敦煌文獻 142 號。

cards.en: From Li Shutong to Master Hongyi
cards.body_en: Li Shutong (1880–1942) taught art and music. In 1918 he became a monk at Hupao Temple in Hangzhou and took the name Hongyi. The record of his life kept by a society in Taiwan lists sutra after sutra that he copied, and says that in his last year he was still writing for students. His last four characters were 悲欣交集, “sorrow and joy together.”
cards.body_zh: 李叔同（1880–1942）原本是美術和音樂老師。民國七年（1918）他在杭州虎跑寺出家，號弘一。弘一大師紀念學會的年表記著他抄過一部又一部的經，直到最後一年還「寫字與晉江中學學生結緣」。他最後寫的四個字是「悲欣交集」。

cards.en: Sutras in the museum, and rooms for copying
cards.body_en: The National Palace Museum keeps a hand-copied scroll labeled “sutra scroll by a Tang copyist”; the museum notes its seventeen characters to a column, the same layout as Dunhuang sutras. Some temples in Taiwan have quiet rooms for copying. One describes the practice as writing out a sutra with the most respectful heart: sit quietly first, and then copy with a calm mind.
cards.body_zh: 台北故宮藏有一卷〈唐人寫經〉；館方指出它「每行書寫十七字」，「與敦煌寫經格式相通」。台灣有些道場設有安靜的抄經堂。佛光山這樣介紹：抄經「即是用最虔敬的心來抄寫佛經」，先靜坐，再「靜心虔誠抄經」。

myths.myth_en: Copying a sutra is a handwriting contest: the prettiest page wins.
myths.myth_zh: 抄經是比賽誰的字漂亮。
myths.fact_en: The point is care and attention, not beauty. Neat, even, and complete matters more than fancy.
myths.fact_zh: 重點是用心和專注，不是漂亮。工整、平均、不漏字，比花俏重要。

myths.myth_en: A sutra page is written from left to right, like this sentence.
myths.myth_zh: 抄經和這行字一樣，由左寫到右。
myths.fact_en: It is written in columns, from top to bottom, and the columns go from right to left.
myths.fact_zh: 抄經是直的寫：每一行由上到下，行由右到左。

myths.myth_en: The Heart Sutra is a very long book.
myths.myth_zh: 〈心經〉是一部很長的書。
myths.fact_en: It is one of the shortest sutras. We counted the main text in Xuanzang's translation: 260 characters. The dictionary says it has “only a few hundred characters.”
myths.fact_zh: 它是最短的經典之一。我們數過玄奘譯本的正文：260 個字。教育部辭典也說它「僅數百字」。

myths.myth_en: Only Buddhists copied holy books by hand.
myths.myth_zh: 只有佛教徒才用手抄經典。
myths.fact_en: Many traditions did. Monks in medieval Europe copied books in a writing room called a scriptorium, Jewish scribes write Torah scrolls with a quill on parchment, and for most of Islamic history the Qur'an was kept in manuscript.
myths.fact_zh: 許多傳統都有。中世紀歐洲的修士在「抄寫室」裡抄書；猶太教的抄寫人用羽毛筆在羊皮紙上寫妥拉；伊斯蘭教的古蘭經，在大部分的歷史裡也是靠手抄本流傳。

tricks.body_en: Same size, in the middle.
tricks.body_zh: 一樣大，寫在正中間。

tricks.title_en: Top to bottom, right to left
tricks.body_en: Start at the top right.
tricks.body_zh: 從右上角開始。

tricks.body_en: Not fast, not fancy.
tricks.body_zh: 不求快，不求花俏。

tricks.body_en: Short enough to copy in one sitting.
tricks.body_zh: 短到可以一次抄完。

safety.en: Ink stains clothes and is very hard to wash out. Wear old clothes or an apron, and roll up your sleeves.
safety.zh: 墨沾到衣服很難洗掉：穿舊衣服或圍裙，袖子捲起來。

safety.en: Cover the desk with old newspaper, and keep the ink in a heavy, steady dish so it will not tip over.
safety.zh: 桌上先鋪舊報紙；墨要裝在重一點、放得穩的碟子裡，免得打翻。

safety.en: Press gently. Crushing the brush against the paper squashes the hairs and can split or break them.
safety.zh: 輕輕地按就好：把筆用力壓在紙上，筆毛會擠扁，也可能分岔或折斷。

safety.en: Do not put the brush, the ink, or the ink stick in your mouth, and do not lick the brush tip to shape it.
safety.zh: 毛筆、墨汁、墨條都不要放進嘴裡，也不要用嘴巴舔筆尖。

safety.en: After writing, wash the brush in clean water until the water runs clear, gently shape it into a point, and hang it tip-down or lay it flat to dry. Wash your hands, too.
safety.zh: 寫完後用清水洗筆，洗到水變清為止；輕輕把筆毛理成尖形，筆尖朝下掛起來或平放晾乾。也要洗手。

materials.en: Squared paper (squares of about 1.5 cm) and a pencil or a fine brush pen
materials.zh: 方格紙（每格大約 1.5 公分）和鉛筆或小楷筆

materials.en: A short text: this lesson's eight characters, or a line the class chooses
materials.zh: 一段短短的文字：這一課的八個字，或全班選的一句話

materials.en: A timer
materials.zh: 計時器

steps.en: Sit up straight, feet on the floor. Take three slow breaths.
steps.zh: 坐正，腳踩在地上。慢慢呼吸三次。

steps.en: For five minutes, copy the text without talking: one character in each square, starting at the top right.
steps.zh: 五分鐘內不說話，把那段文字抄下來：一格一個字，從右上角開始。

steps.en: When the timer rings, stop, even in the middle of a line.
steps.zh: 計時器響了就停，就算一行還沒寫完。

steps.en: Look at your page. Are the first character and the last character the same size? How did the five minutes feel?
steps.zh: 看看自己的那一頁。第一個字和最後一個字一樣大嗎？這五分鐘感覺怎麼樣？

activities.tip_en: Any respectful text works: a poem, a class promise, or a favorite sentence. Students should feel free to choose.
activities.tip_zh: 抄什麼都可以，只要是值得珍惜的文字：一首詩、班級公約、一句喜歡的話。讓學生自己選。

materials.en: Two sheets of squared paper for each student
materials.zh: 每人兩張方格紙

materials.en: A stopwatch
materials.zh: 碼表

steps.en: Copy the eight characters as fast as you can. Write down your time.
steps.zh: 用最快的速度抄那八個字。記下時間。

steps.en: Copy them again, taking at least three times as long.
steps.zh: 再抄一次，至少花三倍的時間。

steps.en: Put the two pages side by side. Circle any character that left the middle of its square.
steps.zh: 把兩張並排。把沒有寫在格子正中間的字圈起來。

steps.en: Talk about it: when is fast writing useful, and when is slow writing better?
steps.zh: 討論：什麼時候寫快比較有用？什麼時候寫慢比較好？

activities.tip_en: Lesson 7 showed that fast scripts have their uses too. Slow is right for this job, not for every job.
activities.tip_zh: 第七課說過，寫得快的字體也有它的用處。「慢」適合這件事，不是每件事都要慢。

sources.en: The Heart Sutra, translated by Xuanzang of the Tang dynasty (Taisho vol. 8, no. 251). We counted the main text: 260 characters. The line 色即是空，空即是色 is quoted from this text.
sources.zh: 《般若波羅蜜多心經》，「唐三藏法師玄奘譯」（大正藏第 8 冊 No. 251）。正文自「觀自在菩薩」至咒語末字，我們數過是 260 字；「色不異空，空不異色，色即是空，空即是色」引自此本。
sources.src: CBETA 電子佛典集成（CC BY-NC-SA 4.0）

sources.en: The Heart Sutra: one roll, only a few hundred characters, one of the most widely read sutras
sources.zh: 般若波羅蜜多心經：「一卷。僅數百字…是漢、藏佛教最流行的經典之一。也稱為『般若心經』、『多心經』、『心經』。」
sources.src: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》「般若波羅蜜多心經」

sources.en: The Diamond Sutra on writing out, keeping, reading, and reciting the text
sources.zh: 《金剛般若波羅蜜經》：「何況書寫、受持、讀誦、為人解說。」
sources.src: CBETA 電子佛典集成 T08 No. 235

sources.en: Before printing, books depended on clerks and copyists; Buddhist sutra copyists in the Northern Wei were called jingsheng
sources.zh: 「印刷術發明以前，古代的典籍都有賴書吏或經生抄寫」「佛教的寫經生，在北魏時期稱作『經生』」
sources.src: 崔中慧〈佛教初期寫經坊設置蠡測〉，《臺大佛學研究》第 32 期（2016）

sources.en: The stone chamber at Dunhuang: found in 1900, full of hand-copied Buddhist texts from the Six Dynasties to the Five Dynasties
sources.zh: 敦煌石室：「內藏六朝、隋、唐及五代人手寫佛教經典及其他藝術品甚富…清光緒二十六年發現，所藏多為英人斯坦因及法人伯希和先後擇要蒐羅而去。」
sources.src: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》「敦煌石室」

sources.en: Ruled black columns on a scroll (烏絲欄); small regular script (小楷)
sources.zh: 烏絲欄：「畫於卷冊或織於絹素的黑色界格。」小楷（106786）：「小而端正整齊的楷書。」
sources.src: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》「烏絲欄」

sources.en: Hongyi (1880–1942): became a monk at Hupao Temple, Hangzhou, in 1918
sources.zh: 弘一：「（西元1880～1942）…民國七年在杭州從虎跑寺了悟和尚出家」；李叔同（61875）：「法名演音，號弘一」
sources.src: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》「弘一」

sources.en: Chronology of Master Hongyi: the sutras he copied; writing for students in 1942; his last four characters
sources.zh: 年表：1920 年「寫經…此年寫《金剛三昧經》、《無常經》、《大乘戒經》等多種經文」；1942 年「依舊寫字與晉江中學學生結緣」；「寫『悲欣交集』（此為最後遺墨）四字」
sources.src: 中華民國弘一大師紀念學會〈弘一大師年表〉

sources.en: Hongyi on his own writing: what it shows is plainness, quiet, and ease
sources.zh: 弘一自述其字「所示者平淡、恬靜、沖逸之致」
sources.src: 《美育》第 183 期（國立臺灣藝術教育館）

sources.en: Sutra scroll by a Tang copyist: seventeen characters to a column, the same layout as Dunhuang sutras
sources.zh: 〈唐人寫經 卷〉（贈書000128）：「每行書寫十七字等形式看，亦與敦煌寫經格式相通」
sources.src: 國立故宮博物院典藏資料檢索

sources.en: The National Central Library keeps 142 Dunhuang items
sources.zh: 「國圖館藏敦煌文獻共 142 號」
sources.src: 《國家圖書館館刊》108 年第 2 期

sources.en: A temple's description of sutra copying: sit quietly first, then copy with a calm, respectful mind
sources.zh: 「抄經，有時亦稱爲寫經，即是用最虔敬的心來抄寫佛經」；程序：「抄經前自行靜坐…靜心虔誠抄經」
sources.src: 佛光山抄經堂

sources.en: Medieval Europe: “Manuscripts (handmade books) were often written and illuminated by monks in monasteries.”
sources.zh: 中世紀歐洲：手抄本常由修道院的修士抄寫、彩繪；scriptorium 是「寫字的地方」
sources.src: J. Paul Getty Museum, “The Medieval Scriptorium”

sources.en: Judaism: a Torah scroll begins with parchment, ink, a quill, and a scribe
sources.zh: 猶太教：妥拉經卷由抄寫人用羽毛筆和墨寫在羊皮紙上
sources.src: The Contemporary Jewish Museum, San Francisco

sources.en: Islam: “For most of Islamic history, the Qur'an has been preserved in manuscript.”
sources.zh: 伊斯蘭教：古蘭經在大部分的歷史裡以手抄本保存
sources.src: Victoria and Albert Museum, “Calligraphy in Islamic art”

sources.en: Stroke order and stroke counts: 心 4, 色 6, 即 7, 是 9, 空 8
sources.zh: 筆順與筆畫數：心 4 畫、色 6 畫、即 7 畫、是 9 畫、空 8 畫
sources.src: 教育部《國字標準字體筆順學習網》

sources.en: Taiwan curriculum: regular script with a brush as a supplement (4-Ⅲ-5); appreciating the layout and style of calligraphy (4-Ⅳ-5)
sources.zh: 十二年國教國語文領綱：4-Ⅲ-5「習寫以硬筆字為主，毛筆為輔，掌握楷書形體結構的書寫方法。」4-Ⅳ-5「欣賞書法的行款和布局、行氣及風格。」
sources.src: 國家教育研究院《十二年國民基本教育課程綱要 語文領域—國語文》

sheets.en: A master, an unknown copyist, and a monk
sheets.zh: 一位名家、一位無名的經生、一位法師
sheets.lead_en: Three pieces of real writing, hundreds of years apart. Look at the size of the characters and the spaces between them. Which one looks calmest to you?
sheets.lead_zh: 三件真的墨跡，前後相隔幾百年。看看字的大小和字與字之間的距離。你覺得哪一件看起來最平靜？

order.lead_zh: 這張紙有三行、每行四格。照抄經的順序，一格一格點下去。

tips.en: Start at the top right.
tips.zh: 從右上角開始。

lessons.title: How Is Chinese Calligraphy Different from Western Calligraphy?
lessons.title_zh: 中文書法和西洋書法有什麼不同？
lessons.blurb_en: Chinese and Western calligraphy are both beautiful writing, but the tools are different, and the tools shape the lines. Watch a soft brush and a stiff broad-edge pen write side by side in 3D, turn the nib and see the thick strokes move, guess which tool made each stroke, and try both on two practice pads.
lessons.blurb_zh: 中文書法和西洋書法都是把字寫得美，可是工具不一樣，而工具會決定線條的樣子。在 3D 裡看軟軟的毛筆和硬硬的平頭筆並排寫字，轉一轉筆嘴、看粗的筆畫跑到哪裡去，猜猜每一筆是哪一種筆寫的，再到兩個練字板上各試一次。
lessons.big_idea_en: The tool shapes the line. A Chinese brush is soft, so its line gets thicker when the hand presses harder. The broad-edge pen of Western calligraphy is stiff and flat, and it is held at one angle, so its line gets thicker or thinner only when the pen changes direction.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 工具決定線條。中文書法用的毛筆是軟的，手按得越重，線就越粗。西洋書法的平頭筆又硬又扁，寫的時候筆嘴的角度固定，所以只有換方向的時候，線才會變粗或變細。

lab.title_en: A Soft Brush and a Stiff Pen
lab.title_zh: 軟軟的毛筆，硬硬的平頭筆
lab.how_en: Drag to turn, and scroll or pinch to zoom. On the left, a brush writes 永. On the right, a broad-edge pen writes n, o, a. Watch the numbers: the brush line follows the pressure, and the pen line follows the direction. Then turn the nib with the slider, or make the pen write 永.
lab.how_zh: 拖曳可以旋轉，滾輪或雙指可以縮放。左邊，毛筆寫「永」；右邊，平頭筆寫 n、o、a。看看數字：毛筆的線跟著「按多重」變，平頭筆的線跟著「方向」變。再用滑桿轉一轉筆嘴，或讓平頭筆去寫「永」。
lab.rose_en: The blue shape shows how thick the pen's line is in each direction. Along the gold bar it is thinnest; across the gold bar it is thickest.
lab.rose_zh: 藍色的形狀表示平頭筆往每個方向走，線會有多粗。順著金色短線走最細，垂直金色短線走最粗。

legend.en: Gold bar: the flat edge of the nib
legend.zh: 金色的短線：筆嘴那條扁平的邊

legend.en: Blue shape: how thick the pen line is in each direction
legend.zh: 藍色的形狀：往每個方向走，線會多粗

legend.en: Red grid: the same 25-cm square on both sheets
legend.zh: 紅色格線：兩張紙上一樣大的 25 公分方格

lab.scale_en: A teaching model. Both sheets have the same 25-cm square. The brush writes 永 with our own stroke data from Lesson 3. The pen's letters n, o, a are our own skeletons, built on a round o, and they are not copies of any historical script. The pen's line width is worked out from one rule: nib width times the sine of the angle between the nib's edge and the direction of travel. Real pens also leave fine hairlines and ink blobs that the model does not show. When the pen writes 永, it follows the center lines of the brush strokes, to show what a stiff nib cannot do.
lab.scale_zh: 這是教學用的示意模型。兩張紙上的方格一樣大（25 公分）。毛筆寫的「永」是第三課我們自己的筆畫資料。平頭筆寫的 n、o、a 是我們自己畫的骨架，以圓形的 o 為基礎，不是任何一種歷史字體的複製。平頭筆的線寬只用一條規則算：筆嘴寬 × 筆嘴的邊和行進方向夾角的正弦。真的筆還會留下細絲和墨點，模型沒有畫。讓平頭筆寫「永」的時候，它走的是毛筆筆畫的中心線，用來看硬筆嘴做不到的事。
lab.credit_html: Model, letter skeletons, stroke data, and the writing engine are drawn and programmed by My Culture Connect. · 模型、字母骨架、筆畫資料與寫字引擎由人師教育協會自繪、自寫。

paras: The English word calligraphy comes from Greek, and dictionaries trace it to words for beauty and writing. People in many parts of the world have turned writing into an art. In this lesson we compare two traditions: writing Chinese characters with a brush, and writing the Latin alphabet with a broad-edge pen.

Start with the brush. Its hairs are soft and springy. Press down, and the hairs spread out and the line grows thick. Lift up, and the line grows thin. A calligrapher can change the width anywhere in a stroke, in any direction. You practiced this in Lesson 2.

Now the broad-edge pen. For more than a thousand years in Europe, the main writing tool was a quill, cut from a feather. Scribes cut the tip flat, like a tiny chisel. The writer holds this flat edge at one angle and keeps it there. Pressing harder does almost nothing, because the tip is stiff.

So where do the thick and thin lines come from? From direction. When the pen moves across its own edge, it leaves a wide line. When it slides along its edge, it leaves a line as thin as a hair. In a round letter like o, the line swells and thins by itself as the pen goes around.

The writing moves differently too. Traditional Chinese texts are written in columns from top to bottom, and the columns go from right to left. The Latin alphabet is written in rows from left to right. Chinese is built from thousands of characters, each with its own strokes; English uses twenty-six letters again and again.
Both traditions ask for the same things: steady hands, patient practice, and a good eye for spacing. In this lesson, watch the two tools write side by side, turn the nib, and then try both yourself.
paras_zh: 英文的 calligraphy 這個字來自希臘文，字典把它追溯到「美」和「寫」這兩個字。世界上很多地方的人，都把寫字變成了一門藝術。這一課比較兩個傳統：用毛筆寫中文字，和用平頭筆寫拉丁字母。
先看毛筆。筆毛又軟又有彈性。往下按，筆毛散開，線就變粗；提起來，線就變細。寫字的人可以在一筆的任何地方、往任何方向改變粗細。這是第二課練過的。
再看平頭筆。在歐洲，有一千多年的時間，主要的書寫工具是用羽毛削成的羽毛筆。抄寫的人把筆尖削成平的，像一把很小的鑿子。寫字的時候，這條扁平的邊保持同一個角度不動。再用力按也幾乎沒有用，因為筆尖是硬的。
那麼粗細是怎麼來的？從方向來。筆往「垂直筆嘴」的方向走，留下寬寬的線；順著筆嘴的方向滑過去，只留下頭髮一樣細的線。像 o 這樣圓圓的字母，筆繞一圈，線就自己由粗變細、再由細變粗。
寫的方向也不一樣。傳統的中文是直的寫：一行由上到下，行由右到左。拉丁字母是橫的寫：由左到右。中文由幾千個字組成，每個字有自己的筆畫；英文則是把二十六個字母一再重複使用。
兩個傳統要求的東西其實一樣：穩定的手、耐心的練習，還有對間距的好眼力。這一課，看兩種筆並排寫字，轉一轉筆嘴，再自己兩種都試試看。
questions: What makes a brush line thicker?
What makes a broad-edge pen line thicker or thinner?
In which directions are traditional Chinese texts and the Latin alphabet written?
answers: Pressing down harder: the soft hairs spread out.
The direction the pen moves. Across its flat edge the line is wide; along its edge the line is very thin.
Traditional Chinese texts go from top to bottom in columns, and the columns go from right to left. The Latin alphabet goes from left to right in rows.

vocab.ex: A ruler is a useful tool for drawing straight lines.
vocab.exzh: 尺是畫直線很有用的工具。

vocab.ex: The new shoes felt stiff at first.
vocab.exzh: 新鞋一開始穿起來硬硬的。

vocab.ex: Do not stand too close to the edge of the pool.
vocab.exzh: 不要站得離游泳池邊太近。

vocab.ex: Hold the camera at a different angle.
vocab.exzh: 把相機換一個角度拿。

vocab.ex: The wind changed direction in the afternoon.
vocab.exzh: 下午風向變了。

vocab.ex: We found a white feather on the grass.
vocab.exzh: 我們在草地上撿到一根白色的羽毛。

vocab.ex: The English alphabet has twenty-six letters.
vocab.exzh: 英文字母表有二十六個字母。

vocab.ex: Eating dumplings at New Year is a family tradition.
vocab.exzh: 過年吃水餃是我們家的傳統。

quiz.q: What makes a brush line thicker?
What was a quill made from?
What changes the width of a broad-edge pen's line?
Which way is the Latin alphabet written?
What do both traditions need?

parts.text_en: The hairs spread when you press. The line can swell or thin anywhere, and its ends are rounded or pointed.
parts.text_zh: 一按，筆毛就散開。線可以在任何地方變粗變細，頭尾是圓的或尖的。

parts.text_en: With the nib at 30 degrees, downstrokes are thick and strokes across are thin. The ends of the lines are cut off at a slant.
parts.text_zh: 筆嘴角度 30 度時，豎的筆畫粗、橫的筆畫細。線的頭尾是斜斜切平的。

parts.meta_zh: 同樣的字母，筆嘴 90 度
parts.text_en: Turn the nib upright and everything swaps: now the strokes across are thick and the downstrokes are thin.
parts.text_zh: 把筆嘴轉成直的，全部反過來：橫的筆畫變粗，豎的筆畫變細。

parts.meta_en: The wrong tool for the job
parts.text_en: The pen follows the same path as the brush, but it cannot press. The heavy dot and the swelling tail are gone.
parts.text_zh: 平頭筆走和毛筆一樣的路線，可是它不能提按。那個重重的點、越來越粗的捺都不見了。

lessons.parts_note_en: All four pictures are drawn by the same model you see in 3D. Tap a card to watch it happen.
lessons.parts_note_zh: 四張圖都是用 3D 裡同一套模型畫出來的。點卡片，在模型裡看它怎麼寫。

pad.lead_en: Now write 永 with the brush pad from Lesson 2. Here, slow means thick and fast means thin, or press harder with a stylus. Direction does not matter at all.
pad.lead_zh: 接著用第二課的毛筆練字板寫「永」。在這裡，寫得慢線就粗、寫得快線就細（用觸控筆的話是越用力越粗）。方向完全沒有關係。

tips.en: Draw the same plus sign you drew with the pen. Are the two lines the same width now?
tips.zh: 畫一個和剛才一樣的加號。這次兩條線一樣粗嗎？

tips.en: Make one line that starts thin, gets thick, and ends thin. Could the pen do that in a straight line?
tips.zh: 畫一條「細→粗→細」的線。平頭筆在一條直線上做得到嗎？

tips.en: Trace 永 and watch your press-and-lift curve.
tips.zh: 描寫「永」，看看自己的提按曲線。

culture_cards.eyebrow: History and Taiwan · 歷史與台灣
culture_cards.title_en: A feather for a pen, a man who brought it back, the art prized above all, and letters in Taiwan's schools
culture_cards.title_zh: 用羽毛當筆、把它找回來的人、最被看重的藝術，和台灣學校裡的字母
culture_cards.lead_en: Three things from museums and encyclopedias, and one from Taiwan's own curriculum.
culture_cards.lead_zh: 三件來自博物館和百科全書的事，和一件台灣課綱裡的事。

cards.en: A feather for a pen
cards.body_en: An encyclopedia explains that the quill, the hollow barrel of a bird's feather, was the main writing tool in Europe from the 6th century until the middle of the 19th, and that goose feathers were the usual source. A museum that keeps medieval books adds that scribes also used swan feathers.
cards.body_zh: 大英百科說：羽毛筆（鳥類羽毛中空的羽管）從六世紀到十九世紀中期，一直是歐洲主要的書寫工具，主要用鵝毛。收藏中世紀手抄本的蓋提博物館補充說，抄寫人也用天鵝的羽毛。

cards.en: The man who brought the broad pen back
cards.body_en: By 1900, few people in Britain knew how to write with an edged pen. Edward Johnston (1872–1944) studied old manuscripts, relearned how to cut reeds and quills, and published a famous handbook in 1906. He is credited with starting the modern revival of calligraphy. He also designed the lettering of the London Underground.
cards.body_zh: 到了 1900 年左右，英國已經很少人會用有「邊」的筆寫字。愛德華・約翰斯頓（1872–1944）研究古老的手抄本，重新學會怎麼削蘆葦筆和羽毛筆，1906 年出版了一本很有名的手冊。大家認為現代書法的復興是從他開始的。倫敦地鐵的字體也是他設計的。

cards.en: The art prized above all others
cards.body_en: The Metropolitan Museum of Art describes calligraphy as the visual art prized above all others in traditional China. It points to the brush: unlike a rigid tool such as a ballpoint pen, a flexible hair brush lets the width of a stroke change.
cards.body_zh: 大都會藝術博物館說，在傳統中國，書法是所有視覺藝術裡最被看重的。它特別提到毛筆：和原子筆這類硬的工具不同，有彈性的毛筆能讓一筆的粗細產生變化。

cards.en: Two directions, two kinds of letters
cards.body_en: Taiwan's Ministry of Education sets out both ways of writing Chinese: vertical text runs from top to bottom and right to left, and horizontal text runs from left to right. In English class, the curriculum asks elementary students to write the 26 letters in print form; in junior high they learn to recognize joined-up handwriting too.
cards.body_zh: 教育部規定了中文的兩種寫法：「中文直式書寫及排印，自上而下，自右而左」「中文橫式書寫及排印，自左而右，自上而下」。英語課方面，課綱要求國小「能書寫 26 個印刷體大小寫字母」，國中再學會「辨識連續書寫體大小寫字母」。

myths.myth_en: A broad-edge pen makes thick lines when you press hard.
myths.myth_zh: 平頭筆用力按，線就會變粗。
myths.fact_en: Its tip is stiff. The width depends on direction: wide across the flat edge, thin along it.
myths.fact_zh: 它的筆尖是硬的。粗細看方向：垂直筆嘴走是寬的，順著筆嘴走是細的。

myths.myth_en: All Western calligraphy is written with a stiff pen.
myths.myth_zh: 西洋書法都是用硬筆尖寫的。
myths.fact_en: Not all. Later styles such as copperplate use a flexible pointed pen, and there the thick strokes do come from pressure. This lesson is about the older broad-edge pen.
myths.fact_zh: 不是全部。後來的銅版體（copperplate）這類寫法用的是有彈性的尖頭筆，粗的筆畫就是靠壓力來的。這一課講的是更早的平頭筆。

myths.myth_en: Calligraphy means Chinese writing with a brush.
myths.myth_zh: 書法就是用毛筆寫中文字。
myths.fact_en: The Chinese word 書法 is defined that way in the dictionary. But the English word calligraphy is used for beautiful writing in any script: Latin, Arabic, and many more.
myths.fact_zh: 教育部辭典確實把「書法」解釋成「毛筆字書寫的方法」。不過英文的 calligraphy 指的是任何文字的美術書寫：拉丁字母、阿拉伯文和其他很多文字都有。

myths.myth_en: One tradition is harder or better than the other.
myths.myth_zh: 其中一種比另一種難，或比較高級。
myths.fact_en: They solve different problems with different tools. Both take years of patient practice.
myths.fact_zh: 它們是用不同的工具解決不同的問題。兩種都需要好幾年耐心的練習。

tricks.body_en: Soft brush, stiff pen.
tricks.body_zh: 軟的毛筆，硬的平頭筆。

tricks.body_en: Press for thick, lift for thin.
tricks.body_zh: 按下去粗，提起來細。

tricks.body_en: Wide across the edge, thin along it.
tricks.body_zh: 垂直筆嘴粗，順著筆嘴細。

tricks.body_en: Top to bottom, or left to right.
tricks.body_zh: 由上到下，或由左到右。

safety.en: Ink stains clothes and is very hard to wash out. Wear old clothes or an apron, and roll up your sleeves.
safety.zh: 墨沾到衣服很難洗掉：穿舊衣服或圍裙，袖子捲起來。

safety.en: Cover the desk with old newspaper, and keep the ink in a heavy, steady dish so it will not tip over.
safety.zh: 桌上先鋪舊報紙；墨要裝在重一點、放得穩的碟子裡，免得打翻。

safety.en: Press gently. Crushing the brush against the paper squashes the hairs and can split or break them.
safety.zh: 輕輕地按就好：把筆用力壓在紙上，筆毛會擠扁，也可能分岔或折斷。

safety.en: Do not put the brush, the ink, or the ink stick in your mouth, and do not lick the brush tip to shape it.
safety.zh: 毛筆、墨汁、墨條都不要放進嘴裡，也不要用嘴巴舔筆尖。

safety.en: After writing, wash the brush in clean water until the water runs clear, gently shape it into a point, and hang it tip-down or lay it flat to dry. Wash your hands, too.
safety.zh: 寫完後用清水洗筆，洗到水變清為止；輕輕把筆毛理成尖形，筆尖朝下掛起來或平放晾乾。也要洗手。

materials.en: Two sharp pencils and two rubber bands for each student
materials.zh: 每人兩枝削尖的鉛筆和兩條橡皮筋

materials.en: Plain paper
materials.zh: 白紙

steps.en: Hold the two pencils side by side and tie them together with the rubber bands.
steps.zh: 把兩枝鉛筆並排，用橡皮筋綁在一起。

steps.en: Hold them so that both points touch the paper, with one point a little higher than the other. Keep that angle.
steps.zh: 讓兩個筆尖同時碰到紙，其中一個稍微高一點。保持這個角度不要變。

steps.en: Draw a line down, a line across, and a circle. The two pencil lines are the two edges of a wide pen stroke.
steps.zh: 畫一條直的、一條橫的，再畫一個圓。兩條鉛筆線就是一筆寬線的兩個邊。

steps.en: Write your name in big letters. Where are the two lines far apart? Where do they almost touch?
steps.zh: 用大大的字母寫自己的名字。兩條線在哪裡離得最遠？在哪裡幾乎碰在一起？

activities.tip_en: Do not turn your wrist as you go around a curve. The angle of the two points should stay the same.
activities.tip_zh: 畫彎的地方手腕不要跟著轉。兩個筆尖的角度要從頭到尾一樣。

materials.en: A brush with clean water and newspaper, and the two-pencil pen
materials.zh: 毛筆、清水和舊報紙，還有兩枝鉛筆做的平頭筆

materials.en: A chart with two columns: Brush and Pen
materials.zh: 一張兩欄的表格：毛筆、平頭筆

steps.en: With the brush and water, write 大. Then write the letter A.
steps.zh: 用毛筆蘸清水寫「大」。再寫字母 A。

steps.en: With the two-pencil pen, write the letter A. Then try to write 大.
steps.zh: 用兩枝鉛筆的平頭筆寫字母 A。再試著寫「大」。

steps.en: In the chart, write what each tool does well and what it cannot do.
steps.zh: 在表格裡寫下每一種工具擅長什麼、做不到什麼。

steps.en: Share one sentence with the class that begins: “The tool shapes the line because…”
steps.zh: 和全班分享一句話，開頭是：「工具決定線條，因為……」

activities.tip_en: There is no wrong answer here. The point is to notice what your hand had to do differently.
activities.tip_zh: 這裡沒有錯的答案。重點是發現自己的手做了哪些不一樣的事。

sources.en: A stiff broad-edged pen makes a stroke that tapers from thin to thick to thin; a flexible pen point or brush makes thicks and thins by pressure
sources.zh: 硬的平頭筆寫出的弧線由細到粗再到細；有彈性的筆尖或毛筆則靠壓力在任何地方做出粗細
sources.src: Britannica Kids, “calligraphy”

sources.en: Chinese calligraphy as the visual art prized above all others in traditional China; the flexible hair brush; columns read from right to left
sources.zh: 傳統中國最看重的視覺藝術是書法；有彈性的毛筆能讓筆畫有粗細變化；傳統中文直行、由右至左
sources.src: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, “Chinese Calligraphy” (Dawn Delbanco, 2008)

sources.en: Calligraphy: from Greek words for beauty and writing
sources.zh: calligraphy：源自希臘文的「美」（kallos）與「寫」
sources.src: Merriam-Webster, “calligraphy”

sources.en: 書法 in the Ministry of Education dictionary: the method of writing with a brush; one of the traditional arts
sources.zh: 書法：「毛筆字書寫的方法。…是我國傳統藝術之一。」
sources.src: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》「書法」

sources.en: The quill: the main writing instrument from the 6th to the mid-19th century; goose feathers were the principal source
sources.zh: 羽毛筆：六世紀到十九世紀中期主要的書寫工具；主要用鵝毛
sources.src: Encyclopaedia Britannica, “quill”

sources.en: “Scribes used quill pens made from feathers of a goose or swan.”
sources.zh: 抄寫人用鵝或天鵝的羽毛做的羽毛筆
sources.src: J. Paul Getty Museum, “Making a Medieval Manuscript”

sources.en: Edward Johnston (1872–1944): credited with starting the modern calligraphic revival; Writing & Illuminating, & Lettering (1906); rediscovered how to make and use reeds and quills
sources.zh: 愛德華・約翰斯頓（1872–1944）：現代書法復興的開創者；1906 年出版《Writing & Illuminating, & Lettering》；重新找回削蘆葦筆與羽毛筆的方法
sources.src: Encyclopaedia Britannica, “Edward Johnston”

sources.en: Johnston's own explanation: with the nib's edge parallel to the writing line, the pen makes a horizontal thin stroke and a vertical thick stroke (p. 66)
sources.zh: 約翰斯頓的說明：筆嘴的邊和書寫的橫線平行時，寫出橫細、豎粗的筆畫（第 66 頁）
sources.src: Edward Johnston, Writing & Illuminating, & Lettering (1906), Internet Archive

sources.en: Johnston and the lettering of the London Underground
sources.zh: 約翰斯頓與倫敦地鐵的字體
sources.src: London Transport Museum

sources.en: Black letter (Gothic script): used for manuscript books across Europe from the end of the 12th century; uniform vertical strokes and angular lines
sources.zh: 黑體字（哥德體）：十二世紀末起歐洲手抄本使用的字體；豎畫整齊一致、線條有稜有角
sources.src: Encyclopaedia Britannica, “black letter”

sources.en: Copperplate: writing made with a flexible, pointed metal pen
sources.zh: 銅版體（copperplate）：用有彈性的尖頭金屬筆寫的字
sources.src: Encyclopaedia Britannica, “round hand script”

sources.en: The qalam: the reed pen still used in Arabic calligraphy, its tip sliced off at an angle
sources.zh: qalam：阿拉伯書法至今仍使用的蘆葦筆，筆尖斜切而成
sources.src: Encyclopaedia Britannica, “qalam”

sources.en: Taiwan's rules for the direction of Chinese text: vertical text top to bottom and right to left; horizontal text left to right
sources.zh: 「中文直式書寫及排印，自上而下，自右而左。」「中文橫式書寫及排印，自左而右，自上而下。」
sources.src: 教育部《中文書寫及排印方式統一規定》

sources.en: Taiwan's English curriculum: write the 26 letters in print form (4-Ⅱ-1); recognize joined-up handwriting (3-Ⅳ-1)
sources.zh: 十二年國教英語文領綱：4-Ⅱ-1「能書寫 26 個印刷體大小寫字母。」3-Ⅳ-1「能辨識連續書寫體大小寫字母。」
sources.src: 國家教育研究院《十二年國民基本教育課程綱要 語文領域—英語文》（107 年）

sheets.en: A book of psalms, a teacher's diagram, and a page from another tradition
sheets.zh: 一本詩篇、一位老師的圖解，和另一個傳統的一頁
sheets.lead_en: Three real pages written or drawn with flat-tipped pens. In each one, look for the thick lines and the thin lines. Do they depend on direction?
sheets.lead_zh: 三頁真的東西，都和扁嘴的筆有關。在每一頁裡找找粗的線和細的線：粗細是不是跟著方向變？

items.alt_en: Detail of a page of the Luttrell Psalter, in Gothic script
items.alt_zh: 勒特雷爾詩篇的一頁局部，哥德體

items.zh: 勒特雷爾詩篇，約 1325–1340 年
items.text_en: A book of psalms made in England, written with a quill in Gothic script, also called black letter. Every downstroke is thick and dark, and the short strokes that join them are thin.
items.text_zh: 在英格蘭製作的一本詩篇，用羽毛筆寫的哥德體（又叫黑體字）。每一筆豎畫都又粗又黑，連接它們的短筆畫則很細。

items.alt_zh: 愛德華・約翰斯頓 1906 年書中的圖解：筆嘴，以及它寫出的細橫線和粗豎線
items.en: Edward Johnston's diagram, 1906
items.zh: 愛德華・約翰斯頓的圖解，1906 年

items.text_zh: 愛德華・約翰斯頓研究古老的手抄本，重新教大家怎麼削蘆葦筆和羽毛筆、怎麼用。他在書裡說明：筆嘴的邊和書寫的橫線平行時，橫的筆畫細、豎的筆畫粗。

items.zh: 古蘭經的一頁，十四世紀
items.text_en: Arabic calligraphy uses a reed pen called a qalam, whose tip is sliced off at an angle. It is an edged pen too, though the script runs from right to left.
items.text_zh: 阿拉伯書法用蘆葦削成的筆，叫 qalam，筆尖是斜斜切出來的。它也是一種有「邊」的硬筆，不過字是由右往左寫的。

tool.zh: 這一筆是哪一種筆寫的？
tool.lead_en: Here is one stroke. Was it made with a brush or with a broad-edge pen? Look at the ends of the line, and at where it gets thick.
tool.lead_zh: 這裡有一筆。它是毛筆寫的，還是平頭筆寫的？看看線的兩頭，再看看它在哪裡變粗。

nibpad.lead_en: On this pad your line works like a broad-edge pen: speed and pressure do nothing, and only direction matters. Trace n, o, a, and then turn the nib with the slider.
nibpad.lead_zh: 在這個練字板上，你的線就像平頭筆：快慢和輕重都沒有用，只有方向有用。描一描 n、o、a，再用滑桿轉一轉筆嘴。

tips.en: Draw a plus sign. Which line is thicker, the one down or the one across?
tips.zh: 畫一個加號。直的那一條粗，還是橫的那一條粗？

tips.en: Draw a circle slowly and watch the line swell and thin by itself.
tips.zh: 慢慢畫一個圓，看線自己變粗、變細。

tips.en: Find the direction that gives the thinnest line. It is the direction of the gold bar.
tips.zh: 找出線最細的那個方向——就是金色短線的方向。

lessons.title: Does Brush Writing Help Your Pencil Writing?
lessons.blurb_en: A brush line swells and thins, and a pencil line stays the same width. So what do the two have in common? Watch a brush and a pencil write the same character side by side in 3D, pull a slider to take the thickness away, find the stroke that is off, and write with both tools on one practice pad. This is the last of the fifteen lessons.
lessons.blurb_zh: 毛筆的線有粗有細，鉛筆的線從頭到尾一樣粗。那兩種字有什麼是一樣的？在 3D 裡看毛筆和鉛筆並排寫同一個字，拉動滑桿把粗細拿掉，找出寫歪的那一筆，再用同一個練字板兩種筆都寫寫看。這是十五堂課的最後一課。
lessons.big_idea_en: A brush and a pencil make different lines, but they build the same character. Take away the thick and thin of the brush, and what is left is the structure: the same strokes, in the same order, in the same places. We could not find a study that proves brush lessons make pencil writing better, so this lesson does not promise that. What it shows is the part the two tools share.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 毛筆和鉛筆寫出來的線不一樣，可是搭起來的是同一個字。把毛筆的粗細拿掉，剩下來的就是結構：一樣的筆畫、一樣的筆順、一樣的位置。我們找不到研究能證明「練毛筆會讓鉛筆字變好」，所以這一課不這樣保證。這一課給你看的，是兩種筆共用的那一部分。

lab.how_en: Drag to turn, and scroll or pinch to zoom. A brush and a pencil write the same character at the same time, along the same path. Watch the stroke counter and the two line widths. Then turn on the brush shadow to lay the brush character under the pencil one, or pick another character.
lab.how_zh: 拖曳可以旋轉，滾輪或雙指可以縮放。毛筆和鉛筆同時寫同一個字，走同一條路線。看看現在寫到第幾筆、兩條線各有多寬。再打開「毛筆的影子」，把毛筆字墊在鉛筆字底下，或換一個字試試。

legend.en: Gold frame: the brush's numbers (its width changes with pressure)
legend.zh: 金色框：毛筆的數字（線寬跟著按多重變）

legend.en: Blue frame: the pencil's numbers (its width does not change)
legend.zh: 藍色框：鉛筆的數字（線寬不變）

legend.en: Red grid: the same 25-cm square on both sheets
legend.zh: 紅色格線：兩張紙上一樣大的 25 公分方格

lab.scale_en: A teaching model. Both sheets have the same 25-cm square, far bigger than a real pencil square, so that you can see the lines. The pencil follows the center line of our own brush stroke data, point for point, and its line is drawn 0.3 cm wide at this size. A real pencil line also gets a little darker when you press, which the model does not show. The numbers come from the model, not from measuring anyone's handwriting.
lab.scale_zh: 這是教學用的示意模型。兩張紙上的方格一樣大（25 公分），比真的鉛筆格子大很多，這樣才看得清楚線條。鉛筆走的是我們自己的毛筆筆畫資料的中心線，一點一點都對得上；在這個大小下，鉛筆線畫成 0.3 公分寬。真的鉛筆用力按，線會稍微變黑一點，模型沒有表現這個。數字是模型算出來的，不是量誰的字得來的。
lab.credit_html: Model, stroke data, and the writing engine are drawn and programmed by My Culture Connect. · 模型、筆畫資料與寫字引擎由人師教育協會自繪、自寫。

paras: For fourteen lessons you have followed the brush. But on most days you write with a pencil or a pen. Taiwan's curriculum calls this kind of writing 硬筆字, hard-pen writing, because the tip does not bend the way brush hairs do. So here is a fair question for the last lesson: does brush writing help your pencil writing?

Start with what is different. A brush is soft, so its line swells when you press and thins when you lift. A pencil is hard. Its core is a thin rod of graphite mixed with clay, and it leaves a line of almost the same width from beginning to end. In our model, the brush line in 永 changes from 0.3 to 2.5 centimeters wide. The pencil line stays at 0.3.

Now look at what is the same. In the model, a brush and a pencil write 永 at the same moment. Both make five strokes. Both follow the same stroke order. Both travel the same path, and every stroke lands in the same position on the grid. Take the width away from the brush character, and you get the pencil character. It looks like a skeleton.

Writers have a name for this skeleton: structure, or 間架結構 in Chinese. It means where each stroke starts and ends, how long it is, and how the strokes balance one another. Taiwan's curriculum asks students in Grades 3 to 6 to learn this structure and to write correct, neat hard-pen characters. It also says that in those grades hard-pen writing comes first, and the brush is the helper.

So, does the brush help? Here is an honest answer. We could not find a study that proves brush lessons make pencil writing better, so we will not promise that. What we can say is what the model shows: the two tools share stroke order and structure. A brush character is also big. The curriculum suggests squares of 8 to 12 centimeters for large brush characters, and 1.5 to 2 centimeters for hard-pen writing in Grades 1 and 2, so a stroke in the wrong position is easier to see.

Now try it yourself. Pull the slider and watch the thickness disappear. Find the stroke that is off in the game. Then write with both tools on the pad. The curriculum's advice is simple: aim for correct first, then upright, then neat, and beautiful last. It also says not to practice too much. Good writing is a habit, and you can build it with any tool.
paras_zh: 前面十四課，我們一直跟著毛筆走。可是平常寫字，你用的多半是鉛筆或原子筆。台灣的課綱把這樣寫的字叫做「硬筆字」，因為筆尖不像筆毛那樣會彎。所以最後一課要問一個很實際的問題：練毛筆字，對鉛筆字有幫助嗎？
先看不一樣的地方。毛筆是軟的，一按線就變粗，一提線就變細。鉛筆是硬的。筆芯是石墨混合黏土做成的細條，寫出來的線從頭到尾幾乎一樣粗。在我們的模型裡，毛筆寫「永」，線寬從 0.3 公分變到 2.5 公分；鉛筆的線一直是 0.3 公分。
再看一樣的地方。模型裡，毛筆和鉛筆同時寫「永」。兩個都是五筆，筆順一樣，走的路線一樣，每一筆落在格子裡的位置也一樣。把毛筆字的粗細拿掉，就得到鉛筆字。它看起來像一副骨架。
寫字的人給這副骨架取了名字：結構，也叫「間架結構」。意思是每一筆從哪裡開始、到哪裡結束、有多長，以及筆畫和筆畫之間怎麼互相平衡。台灣的課綱要三到六年級的學生學會間架結構，寫出正確、工整的硬筆字；課綱也說，這幾個年級「習寫以硬筆字為主，毛筆為輔」。
那麼，毛筆到底有沒有幫助？老實說：我們找不到研究能證明「練毛筆會讓鉛筆字變好」，所以不這樣保證。我們能說的，是模型給你看到的：兩種筆共用筆順和結構。還有一點，毛筆字很大。課綱建議大楷毛筆字的格子是 8 到 12 公分見方，一、二年級硬筆字的格子只有 1.5 到 2 公分，所以哪一筆的位置跑掉了，在大字裡比較容易看出來。
現在換你試試。拉動滑桿，看粗細慢慢消失；在小遊戲裡找出寫歪的那一筆；再到練字板上兩種筆都寫寫看。課綱的建議很簡單：先求正確，再求端正，然後工整，最後才是美觀；課綱也提醒，不要練習過度。把字寫好是一種習慣，用哪一種筆都可以養成。
questions: What is the biggest difference between a brush line and a pencil line?
When a brush and a pencil write the same character, what stays the same?
Does this lesson promise that brush practice will make your pencil writing better? Why or why not?
answers: The width. A brush line gets thicker and thinner as the hand presses and lifts. A pencil line stays almost the same width from beginning to end.
The structure: the number of strokes, the stroke order, and the position and length of every stroke.
No. We could not find a study that proves it. The lesson only shows what the two tools share, which is stroke order and structure.
